Five years ago, an important miscarriage of justice occurred. 

The story began in April 2018 when David Sabatini, an MIT, Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI), and Whitehead Institute scientist and professor began a consensual intimate relationship with Dr. Kristin Knouse, a principal investigator with her own lab at the Whitehead. 

By January 2020, David sought to end the relationship, but Knouse apparently did not want it to end.  When David thereafter started a new relationship and Knouse learned about it, she began a secretive campaign to destroy him by attempting to end his career as a scientist.  She did so by damaging his name, reputation, and that of his family with false sexual harassment and other claims, thereby making him unemployable.

Knouse conspired with Dr. Ruth Lehmann, the then- and still current Director (i.e., President) of the Whitehead Institute, in her efforts to destroy Sabatini.  

The record presented in court demonstrated that Dr. Lehmann committed to Knouse in October of 2020 that she would fire David. Dr. Lehmann made this commitment to Knouse before any investigation of the facts had taken place. 

Seven months after committing to fire him, in March of 2021, Dr. Lehmann, on behalf of the Whitehead, hired the law firm of Hinckley, Allen, Snyder (HAS) to undergo an investigation of David.  By July 2021, HAS shared a draft of its conclusions with MIT, HHMI, and the Whitehead, but not with David or his lawyers. 

On the morning of August 19, 2021, David for the first time received the more than 200-page investigative report and a calendar invite for a meeting the following day with Dr. Lehmann, the president of HHMI, and the HR directors of both institutions. The report was riddled with errors and unsupported claims about David and his relationship with Knouse.

When David's lawyer immediately thereafter reached out to Whitehead counsel to ask whether David was about to be fired, they confirmed that he would be terminated at the meeting.  

On the advice of his lawyer, David immediately resigned from HHMI and the Whitehead rather than attend the meeting.  HHMI did not accept his resignation, choosing instead to fire him.  MIT put David on leave and ultimately revoked his tenure.  David thereafter resigned from MIT.

On August 20, 2021, one day after sending David the HAS report and before David had the opportunity to dispute the facts and the conclusions of the investigation, Dr. Lehmann emailed all employees at the Whitehead informing them that David had violated a number of Whitehead policies "including policies concerning sexual harassment."  

The Lehmann public email, David's resignation and firing, and Dr. Lehmann's claims about David's sexual harassment exploded into a major global scandal covered in mainstream, social, and scientific media around the world as it had all of the requisite ingredients:  

An attractive target with David, one of the most important scientists of his generation in line for the Nobel Prize, a purported inappropriate sexual relationship with a younger female colleague, and a political and institutional environment where punishing a man for sexual harassment advanced the career and reputation of the person and/or institution that destroyed the career and reputation of the accused, regardless of the validity of the allegations.

As a result of Knouse's claims, Lehmann's sham investigation, and the media onslaught that followed, David lost all sources of income and his reputation was destroyed.  All prizes he had been previously been awarded were withdrawn.  He was removed from all scientific advisory and other honorary roles other than as a member of our family foundation's (the Pershing Square Foundation's) scientific advisory board.  

When I initially learned of the news about David in the summer of 2021, I hired him as a consultant to the Pershing Square Foundation as I believed our small foundation team would benefit greatly by his insights (and he now had the time to help us), and he needed the money to support his family.

At my request and under a confidentiality agreement, David provided us with many hundreds of pages of documents including texts and other communications with Knouse, the investigative report, and David's responses to the allegations so that we could do our own evaluation of Knouse's claims.  

I and a member of our family office's legal team carefully reviewed the documents.  After a careful review of the empirical documents --  in particular the texts between Knouse and David -- it became abundantly clear that Knouse's actions were that of an angry and jilted lover, not those of a sexually harassed junior colleague.  And the investigative report appeared designed to deliver a pre-ordained conclusion rather than a dispassionate fact-based analysis.

The impact of the firings and the destruction of his career and reputation on David and his family was extraordinarily devastating, so much so that we became increasingly concerned that he might commit suicide. 

[In order to make sure that David's important scientific research would continue, in February 2023, in partnership with an anonymous donor, we funded $25 million to support David launching a new lab.  As you might expect, I was reviled in the press, in scientific journals, and on social media for doing so and for supporting a so-called sex offender.]

On October 20, 2021, David filed suit against Knouse alleging defamation and tortious interference in his career and his contractual arrangements.  Thereafter, Knouse brought counterclaims against David. 

Today, nearly five years to the date of the filing of the suit, he has finally received justice.

Today, a 13-person jury (seven men and six women) of David Sabatini's peers (12 jurors plus an alternate) unanimously determined that David proved that Kristin Knouse defamed him, tortiously interfered with his contractual relationships (his entire career as a scientist), and tortiously interfered with his prospective advantageous relationships (his future employment).  The jury awarded him nearly $10 million in damages including interest.

I went from working with one agent in a chat to sitting in tmux monitoring 6 agents in parallel in my terminal.

And honestly that's about the limit of my brain. I'm constantly switching between them, remembering what each one is doing, checking who's stuck and who needs me. It's exhausting!

I can’t do that with 100 agents. Or 200. Definitely not a swarm of 200k.

The more I work this way, the more obvious it becomes that it's the wrong form factor. Even with a nice UI, I'm not going to click through every agent to figure out what's going on.

What I need is a feed. A command center that tells me what happened, what's stuck, what needs a decision from me and what I should look at next. So let the agents coordinate the work. Bring me in when I can actually help.

I want to run more agents without spending the rest of my life watching them.
